talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit_alchemy.begin: Alchemy? Oh, %1$s, you've come to the right rock! Sit, sit. Everything in the world is made of essences, and you can learn to read them.
You want to know about alchemy? Nobody ever asks! Wonderful. It all starts with learning to see what things are made of.
Ah, a curious one! I've waited years for someone to ask me that, %1$s. Let me tell you how every apothecary begins.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit_alchemy.eager: %1$s! Back again! Tell me everything. No, wait, let me guess what you've been brewing.
Questions? I live for questions! Well, questions and clouds. Mostly questions.
You've got that look, %1$s. The look of someone who's thrown something strange into a pot. Splendid!
Ask, ask! I've written half a library on this and nobody has read a page of it.
Another apothecary! Do you know how lonely it is, knowing all this and having nobody to tell?
Ha! I knew you'd come back. The craft gets its hooks in you, doesn't it?
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit_alchemy.greet: %1$s! I can smell the crucible on you from here! Come up, come up, tell me what you've learned!
A fellow apothecary on my little rock! Mind the edge, and then mind my questions!
Is that essence on your sleeves? It is! Oh, today is a good day.
%1$s, at last! I've had a dozen thoughts about your work and nobody to tell them to!
First, a Scrying Lens: gold for the frame, a pane of glass, a shard of amethyst. Hold it on anything and look a while. Then a Codex to keep your notes in: a book, an amethyst shard and some ink.
Have you opened your Codex properly? What you learn with the lens is insight. Spend it there and the pages start to make sense.

Look at more things! Stones, beasts, flowers, the soup you had for supper. Every new thing you study teaches you something, and some essences only show themselves once you know the ones they're made of.
You need a crucible. Iron and copper, set over a fire and filled with water. Throw anything in once it's hot and it melts into its essences. The Codex will tell you more, if you've the insight.
Salt, sulphur and mercury! The three principles. Your pot can make them solid, if you give it the right thing to work on. Look in the Codex under the crucible.
Orichalc, the alchemist's own metal. Plain iron, dropped into a pot that's rich in metal and something more... arcane. You'll want plenty of it later, trust me.
Stop scooping essence out with phials like a peasant! Set an alembic on your crucible and some jars beside it. It'll sort the essences out for you while you sleep.
Ever wanted a flame that never goes out? Glowstone, light and a little fire, all in the pot. I've had one burning by my bed for nine years.
Lead into gold! Well, iron into gold, a nugget at a time. And seeds into more seeds. The pot can change a thing's nature, if you feed it the right essences.
Have you noticed what your pot loses? It doesn't vanish. It goes into the land around you. Read about flux in your Codex before you learn about it the hard way.
Every apothecary should know how to clean up after themselves. Purifying salts, a purifying draught, a ward stone. Learn them before you need them, not after.
Now the real work begins: infusion! Pedestals in a ring, one in the middle, and a matrix floating two blocks above it. Keep your essence jars close. It drinks from them.
Did your altar spit things at you? Ha! Balance, my friend. Mirror your pedestals. Salt candles help, and so do skulls and ward stones. Magic hates a lopsided room.
If the work leaves you feeling a little... unwell, a runic amulet helps. Gold and orichalc, made on the altar. It bleeds away the worst of it while you carry it.
Ichor. The blood of the old powers, or near enough. A diamond on the altar, ghast tears and orichalc around it, and a great deal of spirit. Everything good after this needs it.
Have you made yourself a rod yet? An artificer's rod and a focus or two: pull things to you, push them away, lift a whole chest and carry it off. My favourite toy.

Golemancy, now there's a craft! A clock, copper, redstone and ichor on the altar, and out walks a little clockwork guardian. Mine folds up and naps when nothing's happening. Feed it copper when it's dented. We didn't think of it first, mind. Some of the old ones are still down there, in the deep places, minding doors nobody's asked them to open.
The enchanting table will take essence instead of all those gems and trinkets, if you know how to ask it. Bring full phials.
Stuck with a bad enchantment? A spellbinding cloth pulls it right out of the thing, and you keep the essence it was made of.
Melt ichor into gold in your pot and you get ichorium. The finest tools ever made. They do get... hungry. Don't let them feed too often.
Ichorcloth robes! Better than any knight's plate against magic, and the flux takes longer to get its teeth into you. Also, they're very flattering.
A lantern that hangs everflames wherever you point it. For people who never want to carry torches again. Light essence is all it eats.

The table has its limits. The altar doesn't, quite. Set an enchanted thing in the middle with a book of the same magic beside it, and you can push it one step further than anyone should. Mind the instability!
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit_alchemy.maste: You know more than I do now. I'm not jealous. I'm a little jealous. Come and tell me what you discover next!
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit_alchemy.worry: Stop. Look at me. Your eyes are wrong, friend. That's the flux in you. Learn to cleanse it, and quickly. Your Codex has the way, if you've studied far enough.
You've let it get into you again, haven't you? A purifying draught for the worst of it. And what goes deepest only lifts with a whole night's sleep somewhere clean, under a full moon.
Can you feel that? The ground here is sick with flux. Purifying salts, a ward stone, anything. Before it spreads.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit_alchemy.whisp: Some say there are pages that only show themselves to those who've heard the whispers. I've never read them. I don't intend to. Don't you go looking either.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit_alchemy.tip.0: A tip: the crucible loses a little of everything you melt. A small price, but it adds up in one place. Move your work about now and then.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit_alchemy.tip.1: Did you know a jar keeps its essence when you break it? Carry your stores wherever you go.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit_alchemy.tip.2: Tipping out a crucible in a hurry is the fastest way to ruin a meadow. Draw it off into phials instead.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit_alchemy.tip.3: Things that are made from other things carry their essences along. Study the parts and you'll guess the whole.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit_alchemy.tip.4: Creatures have essences too. Hold your lens on a sheep sometime. It's very calming. For you, not the sheep.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit_alchemy.tip.5: The Blood Moon makes flux spread like wildfire. If you've been careless, that's the night you'll pay for it.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit_alchemy.tip.6: Wisps? Little purple lights that drift toward you at night? Don't let them touch you. One good swat does for them.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit_alchemy.tip.7: The pot only works once it's properly hot. Lava under it is quickest, but a campfire will do.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit_alchemy.tip.8: Compound essences are made of two others. Learn the simple ones first and the rest follow.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit_alchemy.tip.9: I once infused a sword with no candles about. I still have the scar. And the sword, actually, so it worked out.
There is a light in the grit off the Maw's rim: dust that still shines a little. Grind a star metal ingot with it, set a spyglass in the middle of an infusion, and you will have a lens that sees what lies ahead of your pod. Fallen stars leave the metal. I can sell you the dust.
